Embedding the ENGS 28 board simulator

This page shows how a textbook page (or any site) can embed the simulator in an <iframe>. The simulator is a plain static app: it needs no special headers (no cross-origin isolation), makes no external requests, and runs entirely in the browser — so it embeds anywhere.

Seeded with a built-in example (?example=blinky)

The simplest embed: pick a built-in example by id. Compact chrome via ?embed=1; the “⤢ Full screen” button pops the current program into its own tab.

<iframe src="…/index.html?embed=1&example=blinky"
        style="width:100%;height:660px;border:0"></iframe>

Seeded with a starter file (?src=…)

For exercise-specific starter code, point ?src= at a .c file (same convention as the C-Programming coding window).

Seeding options, in precedence order

  • ?code=<base64url> — a full program encoded in the URL (what “⤢ Full screen” produces).
  • ?src=<url> — fetch starter code from a .c file.
  • ?example=<id> — a built-in example (blinky, blinky-delay, external-led-d4, button-onboard, button-external).
  • ?embed=1 — compact layout for narrow iframes.
